note: In [L] Taylor jets are read from smoothness on healthy configurations (Germ.computed, RegFit.smooth), and the healthy indicator appears only as the outer factor masked t X f (Plate.Prints.regular, Push.Local.rebate). The difference: the claim that indicators are never differentiated is built into the types, with smoothness asked only of the unmasked function, rather than stated as a lemma.

snippet.text:
lemma computed {U:Support n}{f:Config G n→ℂ}{B:BudgetPoint}(hf:B.Regular U f)(o:Site n)(h:d≤B.order) : JetTest A o (label A o f d) f := by
    have he:=read_projection A o d f hf.symmetry ((hf.smooth _ (one_healthy U _ B.threshold_pos.le)).of_le (Nat.cast_le.mpr h))
    unfold label; rw [dif_pos he.exists]; exact Classical.choose_spec he.exists

proof_context.conclusion: The degree-d jet label of a B.Regular function is read from its smoothness at the flat configuration, which is healthy (one_healthy).

    RegFit E 0 d Y b U→ (E).p.supBounds 0 b U t→ Span B H N p m Y (tell (P.tint i U)) (masked (E).p.threshold b U) 0 0 S X (Extra.Histories.salary (E) b U) 0 (ζ*x) (ζ*x) (2*x)

proof_context.conclusion: Regular marks enter as the masked threshold factor masked b U, with RegFit (smoothness, anchor, unit-null, degree-d projection vanishing) required of the chart function U only.

snippet.text:
def rebate (o : Site n) (X : Support n) (t : ℝ) (f : Config G n → ℂ) :=
  masked t X f - primary T o t (weighted H F o X t f) - masked t (joint T o X) (residual H T o X t f)

proof_context.conclusion: rebate subtracts the primary part and the masked residual from masked t X f, so the healthy mask is always an outer factor applied to unmasked smooth functions.
